newsitem.title: USA: NYH late heat diffs gain on cold, USG prods ease.
newsitem.headline: NYH late heat diffs gain on cold, USG prods ease.

text.p: Differentials on spot New York heating oil edged higher on continued tight supplies and cool weather in the key Northeast market late Thursday, while Gulf Coast prods were mostly weaker, players said.

Crimped supplies of NYH heating oil, combined with talk of snow flurries in New England for Friday and Saturday helped widen prompt diffs about 0.15 cent to between 3.75 and 4.00 cents over May futures, traders said.
The bullish tone was enhanced by an announcement by Sun Co that it would be unable to meet contract commitments until the middle of next week.
But some players cautioned that in a period where demand usually hits the skids, Mother Nature could not be counted on much longer to buttress the heating oil market.
"Unless one of these comets actually hits us, it is very unlikely that cold weather will be a factor at all in two to three weeks," one trader said.
Although East Coast heating oil stocks fell by 252,000 barrels last week, according to the API, they remain 2.2 million above the same week last year.
